chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the earning of the cupper, so he said: There is no problem with it when he does not stipulate (specify wages).
ai.seo_question: Is the earnings of a cupper permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the earnings of a cupper (hijam) provided there is no prior stipulation (musharatah), reflecting the Shia juristic distinction between permissible service fees and prohibited uncertainty or fixed wage contracts in manual trades. This ruling highlights the importance of clear, non-restrictive compensation structures in traditional medical practices, ensuring the transaction remains free from *gharar* (uncertainty) while allowing for fair remuneration.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the earning of the cupper, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it when he does not stipulate (specify wages)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu Basir from who has said the following: “I once asked Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the legal status of earning by means of cupping.
He (the Imam) replied, There is no offense in the earning by such means, if it is not with an established pre-condition.’”
